title: The buddy helper — one promise we cannot keep

steps.headline: The card promises the helper is removed when you uninstall YouCoded. For most Linux users that is not true. What should it say?

options.label: Change the wording, and add a Remove helper button (recommended)
options.summary: The card stops promising automatic removal, and the buddy's settings gain a Remove helper action so anyone can undo it in one click, on any Linux. Downside: one more control in the popup you just approved as a single row — it would only appear once the helper is actually installed, but it is still a new button you have not seen.

options.label: Change the wording only
options.summary: The card says the helper stays until you remove it, and points at KDE's own settings. Nothing new is built. Downside: removing it means digging through KDE System Settings to find a Scripts list, which most people will never do — so in practice it stays forever.

options.label: Keep the promise, clean up where we can
options.summary: We add removal to the three Linux installer formats that support it, and the sentence stays. Downside: it stays FALSE for anyone using the portable AppImage version — the first format we ship — and a leftover entry sits in their KDE settings with no hint of where it came from. It is also fragile on the other three: the cleanup runs as the system administrator and has to reach into each user's personal settings.
